newsitem.title: FINLAND: Russia says NATO expansion would be biggest mistake.
newsitem.headline: Russia says NATO expansion would be biggest mistake.

text.p: Russia launched a fierce attack on NATO expansion on Wednesday, saying on the eve of a summit with the United States that the plan would be the West's biggest blunder since the end of the Cold War.

"President (Boris) Yeltsin and the Russian leadership are convinced that NATO's plans to expand to the east, if realised, could be the West's biggest strategic mistake since the end of the Cold War," Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said.
Yastrzhembsky's comments, at a detailed briefing in Helsinki, set a hostile tone for the summit between Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton in the Finnish capital on Thursday and Friday.
"It is worth thinking again and again; are there really any concrete reasons -- we are sure there are not -- which demand extending the borders of the bloc eastwards?" he said, referring to NATO.

The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation plans to invite a small number of former Soviet bloc countries to join the Western alliance, a proposal Moscow sees as a threat to its security and a move that could upset its relations with the West less than a decade after the fall of the Berlin Wall.
"The very discussion of NATO expansion eastwards has already cast a shadow to a certain extent over relations between the West and Russia, the U.S. and Russia," Yastrzhembsky said.
"I think, much as I would like to be wrong, that we have been robbed to a certain extent of the most valuable achievement of the period since the Cold War -- trust."

NATO's expansion plans are expected to dominate the summit. But Yastrzhemsbky said he still hoped for progress at the talks, which will also cover economic issues and arms control, even if there were unlikely to be any major agreements.
"We would rather expect gradual progress and movement towards mutual strategic goals," he said.
